headline: Sam Stovall flags elevated inflation risk from rising oil prices and high probability of Fed rate hike before year-end under new Chair Walsh
reasoning: Stovall notes oil prices have moved back up from the $60/barrel WTI area, raising inflationary concerns and complicating the central bank outlook. He points to a historical pattern where new Fed chairs have raised rates as their first move — occurring every time over the last 50 years and eight of the last nine times since World War II. The CME FedWatch tool is now pricing in a greater than 75% probability of a rate hike in September and more than 85% before year-end. Stovall argues investors should be more wary of the macro environment than they were a couple of weeks ago.
quote: Well, I think investors should be more wary than they were a couple of weeks ago when oil prices were moving back into the $60 per barrel area for West Texas Intermediate. The fed has a history of raising interest rates as the first move for a new fed chair. That's happened every time over the last 50 years and eight of the last nine times since World War two. So history is on the side of Fed Chair Walsh likely to raise rates next. Also, the CME fed watch tool now has a greater than 75% likelihood that it'll happen in September and a greater than 85% likelihood that will happen before year end.

headline: Q3 of midterm election years is historically a challenging quarter for US equities, with a 50% probability of a greater-than-5% S&P 500 decline in the second half

The political dynamic — Republicans controlling the presidency and both houses of Congress — historically sees the House switch hands after midterms, potentially creating a stalemate government that has historically performed better, but Q3 volatility is expected in the interim.
quote: Q3 of the midterm election year is quite a challenging quarter. We have found, on average, that ten of the 11 sectors posted negative results on average.
